page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.8xlarge is a high-density local storage server built on KVM virtualization. The system is equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. System memory totals 128 GB, maintaining a ratio of 4 GB RAM per vCPU, alongside a baseline network bandwidth allocation of 20 Gbps.

The primary hardware feature of the ecs.d1ne.8xlarge server is its integrated local storage capacity, providing 94,489 GB of direct-attached magnetic HDD storage. Because the storage uses traditional spinning disk drives rather than solid-state flash media, high random IOPS performance is limited, but high-volume sequential read and write throughput is supported directly on the host.

This server architecture provides distinct cost efficiency for storage-dense applications requiring substantial block storage per vCPU without incurring external network storage overhead. The configuration of 32 dedicated cores, 128 GB RAM, and high disk capacity fits large-scale data processing workloads, distributed file systems like HDFS, map-reduce frameworks, warm log archives, and big data warehousing nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.8xlarge is a storage-dense instance optimized for high-capacity data processing and bulk storage requirements. Built on x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it features 32 dedicated vCPUs from Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors operating at 2.5 GHz, paired with 128 GB of system memory and 20 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Its key hardware highlight is 94,489 GB of direct-attached local HDD storage, offering massive block capacity on a single instance. While reliance on spinning disk storage presents IOPS and latency tradeoffs compared to NVMe options, it delivers favorable cost efficiency for sequential read/write operations and high-volume data retention. The balanced ratio of 4 GB RAM per vCPU combined with expansive local disk space makes this server suitable for big data analytics, distributed file system nodes, log aggregation, and large-scale data warehousing workloads.
